quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and your vehicle slides on a layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian notices your vehicle.
Always let pedestrians cross first, even if they are jaywalking.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let pedestrians cross first, even if they are jaywalking.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. Always be alert and yield to all pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in your side mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
Look in your rearview mirror.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulders.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down but stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway begins. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a right curve ahead. Slow down to the speed indicated on the sign (35 mph in this example).

questions.question: A driver can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

options.text: When the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
Anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Low speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force in a crash.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.
Safely change to reverse and go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic. You may receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track:

options.text: Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.
Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one of the tracks is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not start moving as soon as a train passes. Wait until you have a clear view down all tracks before crossing. Even with one track, check again for another train that may be coming.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
Quickly changing lanes and shifting in and out of traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents before they happen. It helps you deal with aggressive, careless, distracted, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is coming from. Immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs about upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs about hazards are yellow with black lettering or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black lettering or symbols.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging in from the right.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and cannot see oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and you can safely make the turn.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when turning so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches the actions of other drivers.
Travels at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches the actions of other drivers.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers are doing and prepares for potential problems.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered crossing gates or sounds of an approaching train.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and drivers cannot see well. You must use your headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with a bicyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for clear traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist should get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for clear traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would any other vehicle, but carefully. Leave at least 3 feet of space from your mirror to the bicyclist, or 5 feet on higher-speed roads. Do not honk unless necessary, as it may startle the rider.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other vehicles pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage. What should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers your plans.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle behind you, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Slow down and let the vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to alert them.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicyclist and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly or too close can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: Which is a trait of a defensive driver?

options.text: Anticipation
Passivity
Easy to distract
Anger

questions.correctAnswerText: Anticipation
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers keep a safe distance from other vehicles. They think ahead about what might happen on the road and take steps to avoid problems.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Learn how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical abilities.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: No action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: A driver extends their left arm and hand downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended downward means the driver plans to stop. Change your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must let the other go first?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This applies to controlled and uncontrolled intersections.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
You can only turn from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. These lanes are for buses and cars with a driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Then turn the wheel to get back onto the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Then turn the wheel to get back onto the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the road, slow down gently with the brakes while the wheels are still off the pavement. When you are going slowly enough, turn the wheel to return to the road. Do not turn the wheel sharply.

questions.question: A driver behind you is tailgating. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually. This lets the tailgater pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, wait until the road is clear ahead and slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others around you?

options.text: It stops other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves sharply right, then left.
The road curves sharply left, then right.
The road curves left.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will curve sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very rare.
Very dangerous.
Not a concern.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to driving prevents crashes.
